syllabusTopics: Saturated hydrocarbons (Alkanes): preparation from haloalkanes (reduction and Wurtz reaction), decarboxylation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkene and alkyne
Chemical properties of alkanes: substitution reactions (halogenation, nitration and sulphonation only), oxidation of ethane
Unsaturated hydrocarbons (Alkenes): preparation by dehydration of alcohol, dehydrohalogenation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkyne
Chemical properties of alkenes: addition reaction with HX (Markovnikov's addition and peroxide effect), H2O, O3, H2SO4 only
Alkynes: preparation from carbon and hydrogen, 1,2-dibromoethane, chloroform/iodoform only
Chemical properties of alkynes: addition reaction with H2, HX, H2O; acidic nature (action with sodium, ammoniacal AgNO3 and ammoniacal Cu2Cl2)
Test of unsaturation (ethene and ethyne): bromine water test and Baeyer's test
Comparative studies of physical properties of alkane, alkene and alkyne
Kolbe's electrolysis methods for the preparation of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Alkynes add like alkenes — twice. **H₂**: Lindlar stops at the alkene, excess Ni gives the alkane. **HX**: HCl over HgCl₂ gives **vinyl chloride**; HBr adds Markovnikov, twice for the full dihalide. **H₂O** (H₂SO₄/HgSO₄): Markovnikov hydration gives the **enol**, which tautomerises — ethyne lands on **acetaldehyde** (the family's only aldehyde), all others on ketones.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Terminal alkynes are weakly acidic (pKa ≈ 25) because of 50% s-character, forming acetylides with metals and giving characteristic precipitates with ammoniacal AgNO3 and Cu2Cl2."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The white and the red*** — one terminal hydrogen, two verdicts: white Ag2C2 with ammoniacal silver, red Cu2C2 with ammoniacal copper — the fastest structure probe in alkyne chemistry.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Add Like an Alkene, Acid Like No Other The C≡C bond adds H₂, HX and H₂O just as C=C does (twice over), but the sp carbons hold their electrons so tightly that a **terminal alkyne hydrogen becomes acidic** — the only hydrocarbon H that metals can replace. That acidity powers the **ammoniacal AgNO₃ and Cu₂Cl₂ tests**.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Addition of H₂ - **HC≡CH + H₂ (Lindlar) → CH₂=CH₂**; **+ H₂ (Ni, excess) → CH₃–CH₃**. - Two π bonds → up to two equivalents of H₂; catalyst choice sets the stop point. ### 2.2 Addition of HX - **HC≡CH + HCl (HgCl₂ catalyst) → CH₂=CHCl** (vinyl chloride — PVC feedstock). - **HC≡CH + HBr → CH₂=CHBr → CH₃CHBr₂** (Markovnikov, twice for internal alkynes).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Hydration: enol → CH3CHO (ethyne only; others ketones). HCl/HgCl2 → vinyl chloride. AgNO3/NH3 white; Cu2Cl2/NH3 red — terminal only. Acidity ladder: alkyne 25 < alkene 44 < alkane 50.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Acetylene is acidic in nature. Explain with a chemical test. (3m)** — **Why acidic:** in ethyne the C–H bond is formed from an **sp hybrid orbital with 50% s-character**; s electrons lie closer to the nucleus, so the carbon **holds its bonding electrons tightly**.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): What is the product of hydration of ethyne and how is it formed?** — Ethyne adds water in the presence of **dilute H₂SO₄ and HgSO₄ catalyst**: the water adds **Markovnikov-fashion** across the triple bond to give **vinyl alcohol, CH₂=CHOH — an enol**.…

rows.text: The NEB 2024 answer needs the s-character reason AND a test equation — quote both the AgNO3 precipitate and its colour.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: s-character is acidity: the sp orbital holds the carbanion's pair close to the nucleus — the only acidic hydrocarbon hydrogens, and the only ones metals can pull off.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Alkyne reactions: H2 — Lindlar stops at alkene, Ni excess gives alkane (2 eq). HX — HCCH + HCl (HgCl2) -> CH2=CHCl (vinyl chloride); +HBr -> CH2=CHBr -> CH3CHBr2 (Markovnikov twice). H2O — HCCH + H2O (H2SO4/HgSO4) -> enol CH2=CHOH -> tautomerises -> CH3CHO (acetaldehyde); internal alkynes -> ketones.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Vinyl chloride from ethyne once fed the entire PVC industry — mercury-catalysed HCl addition at scale.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Distinguish terminal and internal alkynes using ammoniacal reagents.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Ethyne hydration gives an aldehyde, not an alcohol or ketone:** the enol tautomerises all the way to CH₃CHO — the one aldehyde in the family.  ·  **Only terminal alkynes give precipitates:** internal alkynes have no ≡C–H — a negative AgNO₃ test is informative, not a failure.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Acidity is relative:** pKa 25 is "acidic" only next to 44 and 50 — water and alcohols are far stronger acids.  ·  ## 7.
